minutes.headline: Finance Committee approved August minutes and reviewed financial policies ahead of an October 11 joint meeting with Selectmen.
minutes.summary: The committee approved two sets of prior minutes, heard a resident challenge how a committee vacancy was filled, and reviewed financial policies the Board of Selectmen wants to revisit: debt service and the definition of regular tax levy, free cash priorities, the stabilization funds, and OPEB for new personnel. Liaison assignments and department updates were also covered.

budget_items.topic: Road maintenance funding and pothole fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Free cash priorities were first set when roads were a big deal; with the pothole fund and annual deposits toward a goal, free cash can be redirected.
Policy keeps the stabilization balance at a percentage of the omnibus budget; members debated whether the capital stabilization fund counts within it.
Proposal to add the cost of beginning to fund OPEB for any new personnel into the operating budget.

Agreed to raise at the joint meeting whether to segregate the capital stabilization fund from the 5% minimum policy.
Michele to act as liaison to the Lunenburg Public Library.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee reviewed financial policies the Board of Selectmen wants to revisit, including debt service, free cash, stabilization and OPEB, and reached no resolution.
A joint meeting with the Board of Selectmen is planned for October 11 at 6:30, with the warrant article public hearing at 7:30.
Members agreed to raise at the joint meeting whether the capital stabilization fund should be set apart from the 5% minimum stabilization policy.
A resident said town counsel's response shows the 30-day clock never started, because written notice of the vacancy was not given, so the filling of the vacancy was flawed.
The committee approved two sets of prior minutes and named Michele as liaison to the Lunenburg Public Library.

why_it_matters: The policies under review decide how much free cash goes to roads and how large a reserve the town holds, which shapes what the tax bill must cover and how much is left for capital needs.
Adding the cost of funding OPEB for new personnel to the operating budget would add a recurring cost to the town budget, mostly taxes, in future years.
watch_next: October 11 joint meeting of the Finance Committee and Selectmen at 6:30, with the warrant article public hearing at 7:30.

They differ on the road set-aside: ours says $50,000 and the official minutes say $50K each year. The planned joint meeting and the library liaison appear only in ours, and the vertex presentation and borrowing-policy review appear only in the official minutes.
